output.summary: The nightly endurance job failed for three consecutive days due to the consecutive-error gate tripping on the qwen2.5:0.5b model. The proposed solution is to switch to using the qwen2.5:1.5b model instead.
The decision is that clerk jobs will send think=false to every local model, owned by Swapnil with a deadline of 2026-10-20. A per-job thinking flag was discussed but rejected.

INC-2209: Between 10:02 and 10:19 UTC, the backup task failed to write an archive due to a full data disk (0 bytes free), but after removing an old 9 GB log file, the 10:30 run succeeded with no data loss.

Four cloud models achieved perfect scores of 50/50, including Mistral Large 3, Qwen3-Coder-480B, and two Kimi variants. Local models performed significantly worse, with the default local model scoring only 18/50 and qwen2.5-coder:7b achieving 37/50 but with substantially higher latency.

The backup readiness gate was updated from a fixed string check to dynamically verify both recent archives and active scheduling through Windows Task Scheduler or crontab, preventing false positives from one-time archives that wouldn't continue running.
Run 20261012T043600 attempted 150 targets, all of which were comparable.

output.disagreement_summary: Analysis A attributes the timeouts to the 420-second model limit, while Analysis B claims they are caused by pytest grading exceeding 120 seconds.

Analysis A recommends keeping qwen2.5-coder:7b as the clerk because it passed every test on the first attempt, while Analysis B suggests switching to granite4.2:8b due to its specialized capabilities in extraction and classification tasks.

Analysis A concludes that the memory store is the bottleneck because only 11 lessons were admitted, while Analysis B argues that the model itself is the bottleneck since a 30B model cannot effectively utilize the lessons.
Analysis A recommends merging #484 with a squash and re-gathering organ 37 afterwards, while Analysis B suggests merging #484 with a merge commit to maintain reachability of the cited commit.
Analysis A recommends Kimi K3 for teaching due to its status as the newest model, while Analysis B suggests Qwen3-Coder-480B because it excels in coding speed.
Analysis A recommends running the Docker drill tonight, while Analysis B suggests waiting until both judged runs finish due to Docker's potential 8 GB RAM usage.
